bib.title: Python Data Science Handbook, Chapter 5: Machine Learning

question: How do data scientists use scikit-learn to build, validate, tune and interpret supervised and unsupervised models in practice?
contributions: Vocabulary of supervised/unsupervised learning, classification, regression, clustering, dimensionality reduction
The scikit-learn Estimator API and data layout
Validation, learning curves, bias-variance and grid search
Hands-on treatments of naive Bayes, linear regression, SVM, random forests, PCA, manifold learning, k-means, GMM, KDE and a HOG face-detection pipeline

limits: Chapter is explicitly not a comprehensive ML introduction or scikit-learn manual (p.331).
Most accuracies are single runs on small built-in datasets (Iris 150, digits 1797, LFW 1348) with one random split; no seeds varied, no confidence intervals.
Hyperparameter-search best scores (KDE classifier 0.967, LinearSVC 0.987) are the maximum over the search, not held-out estimates.
Face detector is a prototype: weak negatives cause false positives, one scale, no non-max suppression; author says HOG is no longer state of the art and points to deep learning.

Code uses 2016-era APIs that no longer run unmodified (reader knowledge, not in the source): sklearn.cross_validation, learning_curve and grid_search modules (now model_selection), GMM (now GaussianMixture, with covariances_), Imputer (SimpleImputer), RandomizedPCA (PCA(svd_solver='randomized')), LinearRegression(normalize=...), fetch_mldata (fetch_openml), grid_scores_ (cv_results_), get_feature_names (get_feature_names_out), samples_generator import path, KFold/LeaveOneOut signatures; plus pandas resample(how=), pd.datetime, matplotlib normed=True and plot(hold=), seaborn size=, cmap 'spectral', skimage hog(visualise=), Basemap.
Printed prose and outputs disagree in places: digits GNB 0.833 called 'about 80%'; face detector prints 33.0 detections, text says 30; Fig 5-17 caption says k-means but the code is GMM.
practices: Never validate on the data the model was fit on; a 1-NN gets 1.0 that way (Model validation the wrong way).
Use a holdout set, or k-fold/leave-one-out cross-validation when data are scarce (Model validation via cross-validation).

Diagnose with validation curves (score vs complexity) and learning curves (score vs training size); once train and validation curves converge, more data will not help, only a different model (Learning Curves).
Underperforming estimator: try more or less flexible model, more samples, or more features; the answer is often counterintuitive (Selecting the Best Model).
Tune several hyperparameters with GridSearchCV; if the optimum falls on the grid edge, expand the grid (Grid Search; SVM face example).
Do not encode categories as integers; use one-hot (DictVectorizer, OneHotEncoder) with sparse output when cardinality is high (Categorical Features).
Weight word counts with TF-IDF for text classifiers (Text Features).
Chain imputation, feature transforms and the estimator in a make_pipeline so the steps apply together (Feature Pipelines).
Start classification with Gaussian or multinomial naive Bayes as a fast baseline (When to Use Naive Bayes).
Regularise basis-function regressions with Ridge (L2) or Lasso (L1, sparse); choose alpha by cross-validation (Regularization).
Bootstrap resampling gives coefficient uncertainty when using a linear model interpretively; scikit-learn itself offers no parameter inference, use StatsModels (Estimator API; bike example).
Tune SVM C by cross-validation; use PCA before SVM for high-dimensional pixels (SVM, Face Recognition).
Average many randomised trees (bagging / random forest) to cure single-tree overfitting (Random Forests).
Start high-dimensional exploration with PCA before manifold methods; pick component count from the cumulative explained-variance ratio (PCA Summary; Manifold Learning).
Run k-means with several initialisations (n_init defaults to 10) because EM finds only local optima (k-Means caveats).
Treat GMM primarily as a density estimator and pick component count by AIC/BIC or cross-validated likelihood (GMM, How many components).
Choose KDE bandwidth by cross-validated log-likelihood (leave-one-out for small samples) (KDE).
Subclass BaseEstimator and a Mixin for custom estimators; __init__ only assigns named args, fit returns self, learned attributes end in underscore (KDEClassifier anatomy).
Use hard negative mining and multi-scale windows to improve a sliding-window detector (Face Detection, Caveats).

train_score, val_score = validation_curve(PolynomialRegression(), X, y,
                                          'polynomialfeatures__degree',
                                          degree, cv=7)

param_grid = {'polynomialfeatures__degree': np.arange(21),
              'linearregression__fit_intercept': [True, False],
              'linearregression__normalize': [True, False]}
grid = GridSearchCV(PolynomialRegression(), param_grid, cv=7)

pca = RandomizedPCA(n_components=150, whiten=True, random_state=42)
svc = SVC(kernel='rbf', class_weight='balanced')
model = make_pipeline(pca, svc)
param_grid = {'svc__C': [1, 5, 10, 50],
              'svc__gamma': [0.0001, 0.0005, 0.001, 0.005]}
grid = GridSearchCV(model, param_grid)
